title: Admin SatNav: Runbook Orchestrator and Route-aware Shortflow Executor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'SatNav' orchestration layer that maps incident signals to curated runbook sequences (shortflows), executes them with parameter binding and RBAC gating, and exposes a safe dry-run and audit trail. Purpose: reduce mean time to resolution for common support scenarios, make runbooks first-class composable tasks, and enable safe incremental automation that non-engineering support can trigger with guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: SatNav can resolve incoming incident tags to a runbook sequence using a config-driven matcher
Operators can execute a runbook sequence in dry-run mode with no side effects and a computed risk score
Execution logs and parameter provenance appear in Console under a new 'SatNav executions' view
RBAC prevents escalation: only users with 'runbook.execute' can run steps that require secrets or privileged APIs
Can fallback to manual step-by-step execution if a step fails or a circuit-breaker trips
steps: Design: define runbook schema (steps, inputs, outputs, idempotency annotations)
Mapper: implement rule-based matcher + ML-label fallback to pick a shortflow for an incident
Executor: sandboxed task runner with dry-run mode and simulators for privileged actions
Safety: risk scoring, circuit-breakers, automatic rollback markers, and audit logging
Console: UI surface to preview route, parameters, and playback logs
Telemetry: instrument events for routing accuracy, run success, latencies, and human overrides
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha: Kickoff; scoped MVP to top-10 incident tags by frequency (pager, quota, evictions)
2026-03-03 - Marco: Prototype of rule matcher implemented; added YAML schema for shortflows in repo
2026-03-05 - Design review with SRE and Support: require dry-run + risk score before any automated remediation
2026-03-07 - Security: flagged secret-bridge integration for formal security review; gating added to plan
2026-03-09 - Marco: End-to-end demo using a simulated quota-exhaustion incident; observed 60% time reduction versus manual triage
2026-03-10 - PM: Request to include easy rollback labels and step-level runbook owner metadata
notes: Trade-offs considered: full ML-based routing vs rule-first matcher. Chosen rule-first with ML fallback to keep behavior inspectable and auditable. Executor will initially support a safe whitelist of actions (status checks, tagging, scaled down control plane manipulations). Secret-using steps will be proxied through a privileged execution service requiring additional approval.
blockers: Pending security review for secret proxy and formal sign-off on RBAC policies; need a shortlist of 10 canonical shortflows from Support and SRE teams.
next_steps: 1) Complete security review (target 2026-03-17) 2) Implement console preview and dry-run UI (2026-03-24) 3) Run closed beta with Support on 3 incident types (quota, node-eviction, model-deploy-failure)
risks: Over-automation could cause accidental remediation; mitigate with dry-run, risk scores, and mandatory human confirmation for high-risk steps. Mapping accuracy could mis-route incidents; monitoring and fast rollback paths required.
observability_plan: Emit satnav.route.match, satnav.execution.start, .step.success, .step.fail, .execution.rollback as structured events. Add dashboards for routing accuracy, step latencies, and human override rate. Tie regression alerts to runbook-flake thresholds.
postmortem_plan: If an automated runbook causes customer impact, run a 3-step postmortem: (1) immediate disable of offending shortflow, (2) capture execution trace and playbook inputs, (3) root-cause and retro with Support and Security to tighten gating
